q: Minimising squared error gives the ML hypothesis when the noise is:
options: Gaussian with mean 0 and fixed variance
Absent from the inputs and targets only by chance
explain: Taking the log of the Gaussian likelihood leaves exactly the sum of squared errors to minimise.

q: Why can we maximise the log likelihood instead of the likelihood?
options: The logarithm is increasing, so the maximiser does not change
Logs make the result always positive
It gives a different and better hypothesis
explain: The same h maximises both, and the log turns the product into an easier sum.
